name: Hartley Rogers
current_role: Co-Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board, Hamilton Lane (Nasdaq: HLNE) (named co-CEO Oct 2026)
profile: Private-equity veteran who joined Hamilton Lane in 2003/04 after two decades at Morgan Stanley and Credit Suisse; owns a large stake (>13% per Forbes) in the private-markets firm, which listed on Nasdaq in 2017. In Oct 2026 he was named co-CEO alongside Juan Delgado-Moreira while remaining board chairman; Erik Hirsch became executive co-chairman.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Advisory Board of HarvardX (Harvard's online-learning initiative) and sits on the boards of the Institute of International Education and Bessemer Securities; previously on the Metropolitan Opera board.
deep_cut_fact: His father, Hartley Rogers Jr., was an MIT mathematics professor (1956-2009) and a founder of computability theory, author of the classic 'Theory of Recursive Functions and Effective Computability'; the MIT obituary lists son Hartley R. Rogers.
notes: Press contact Tia Wilson; IR John Oh (Hamilton Lane). Good finance/private-markets angle; firm has infrastructure & real-assets strategies relevant to energy/data centers.

name: Yang Aihua
current_role: Founder and Executive Director, Autostreets Development Ltd (HKEX: 2443), Shanghai used-car auction platform
profile: Shanghai auto-retail entrepreneur who founded Baoxin Auto in 1999, built it into one of China's largest BMW dealer groups and listed it in Hong Kong in 2011. In late 2015 he sold control to China Grand Auto (now Grand Baoxin) and in 2014 founded Autostreets, a B2B used-car auction platform that listed in Hong Kong; he remains an executive director.
interesting_fact: Baoxin opened its first 4S store in Shanghai in 1999 as one of Audi's first authorized dealers in China, and in 2004 became one of BMW's first authorized dealers, later the world's largest BMW dealer group.
deep_cut_fact: Autostreets counts Cox Automotive, parent of US wholesale auction giant Manheim, as its second-largest shareholder, alongside Tencent and JD.com; by 2022 about 4,900 dealerships had sold used cars through the platform.
notes: Described in press as extremely low-profile and rarely interviewed. Best route is via Autostreets corporate channels (company site / HKEX filings). Autostreets chairman is Yang Hansong.

name: Luo Yi
current_role: Co-owner (about 22% of Chongyang Group per Tianyancha, as reported), Shanghai Chongyang Investment, with husband Qiu Guogen
profile: Luo Yi and her husband Qiu Guogen control Shanghai Chongyang Investment, one of China's oldest and largest private securities funds, founded in 2001 and known for long-term value investing. The couple appear jointly on the Hurun Global Rich List (RMB 7.5bn in 2026). Qiu runs investments; Luo keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Before founding Chongyang, the couple reportedly grew their wealth nearly 20-fold in the 1996-97 bull market by buying undervalued stocks such as Shenzhen Development Bank.
notes: Almost no public information about Luo Yi personally; she appears only as co-listed with Qiu Guogen. Approach via Chongyang Investment (Shanghai). Site is behind a qualified-investor gate; no published press email found.

name: Lou Zhongfu
current_role: Co-founder and honorary chair, Guangsha Holding Group (Hangzhou); son Lou Ming is chairman
profile: Dongyang, Zhejiang native (b. 1954) who rose from construction worker to head the collective Dongyang construction company in 1984 and built it into Guangsha, a Hangzhou-based construction, real-estate and media conglomerate. He handed the chairmanship to his son Lou Ming; in 2021 Dongyang state capital took control of listed Zhejiang Guangsha.
interesting_fact: He joined Dongyang No. 3 Construction Company in 1973 as a worker and rose via materials-department head to general manager, the business that became Guangsha.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988 he was named a national 'collective construction entrepreneur of the new era', and in 1997 a national outstanding enterprise manager.
notes: Not a good outreach target: detained by CCDI in late 2014/2015 in connection with the Ling Jihua case and named in a 2022 bribery trial; no recent public appearances found (alive status not confirmed after 2022). Family lost control of listed Zhejiang Guangsha in 2021.

name: Markus Hannebauer
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, think-cell Software GmbH (Berlin)
profile: Computer scientist with a TU Berlin PhD in artificial intelligence who, after working at Fraunhofer, co-founded think-cell with Arno Schödl in Berlin in 2002. Its PowerPoint charting add-on became a standard tool in consulting and finance with over one million users; PE firm Cinven bought a majority stake in 2021. He ran the company as CEO until March 2024 and now chairs the board.
interesting_fact: think-cell won the Berlin StartUp award in its very first year (2002) and two decades later passed one million users worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he published a Springer book (Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 2427), 'Autonomous Dynamic Reconfiguration in Multi-Agent Systems', introducing 'agent melting and splitting', with a case study on medical appointment scheduling.
notes: info@think-cell.com is the company's general contact, not personal. LinkedIn link taken from Indezine profile page (not independently verified as his). AI/software founder angle; relatively accessible to tech press historically.

name: Qiu Lingyun
current_role: Former board secretary of Smoore International (HKEX: 6969); not listed among senior management in the 2025 annual report
profile: Smoore early executive (male, b. c.1975) whose fortune came from his stake in Smoore International, the world's largest maker of vaping devices and components (clients include BAT, Japan Tobacco, NJOY), which listed in Hong Kong in July 2020. He was CFO of Smoore Shenzhen 2011-2016, then board secretary handling board matters and investor relations.
interesting_fact: Smoore's 2020 Hong Kong IPO briefly made several of its early managers billionaires; Qiu appeared on the Forbes list only in 2021, after the shares peaked.
deep_cut_fact: He studied industrial international commerce (engineering degree) at Shanghai University, graduating in 1999, and earned an executive MBA from CEIBS in 2015.
notes: Very low profile; appears to have left the Smoore management team (absent from 2025 annual report). Smoore's IR mailbox IR@smooreholdings.com exists but is the company's, not his. Vaping is a sensitive sector.

name: Gustavo
profile: Record refers to Venezuelan media magnate Gustavo Cisneros (listed jointly with brother Ricardo Cisneros, Forbes 1996), chairman of Organización Cisneros and co-founder of Univision. He died on 29 December 2023 in New York, aged 78, as announced by Cisneros.
notes: Deceased 29 Dec 2023. Source: https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/billionaire-gustavo-cisneros-who-defined-venezuela-business-dies-at-78-123123000091_1.html (Reuters) and https://as-coa.org/articles/remembering-gustavo-cisneros-1945-2023. Group now led by daughter Adriana Cisneros (CEO since 2013).

name: Boris Titov
current_role: Russian Special Presidential Envoy for Relations with International Organizations on the Sustainable Development Goals (since 2024); owner of Abrau-Durso winery group
profile: Moscow-born (1960) MGIMO economist who co-founded oil/petrochemicals trader Solvalub (SVL Group) in 1991 and later bought the historic Abrau-Durso sparkling-wine house. Led the Business Russia lobby, served as Russia's first business ombudsman (2012-2024 per most sources), founded the Party of Growth, and ran for president in 2018 (0.76%). Since 2024 he is Putin's special envoy on SDGs.
interesting_fact: He ran in Russia's 2018 presidential election as the Party of Growth candidate, finishing sixth with 0.76% of the vote.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989 he headed the chemicals department of Urals, a Soviet-Dutch joint venture, and in 1991 he and partners set up Solvalub by buying a London-based solvents and lubricants firm they had worked with alongside Soviet oil exporter Soyuznefteexport.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (incl. 2025 director-disqualification sanction re Abrau-Durso; listed on OpenSanctions). Russian state official. Outreach likely inappropriate/legally sensitive for a Western podcast; no personal contacts researched.

name: Kong Lingyong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Dynanonic Co. (SZSE: 300769), lithium-battery cathode materials
profile: Born 1978, a professor-level senior engineer and co-founder (2007) of Shenzhen Dynanonic, a leading maker of nano lithium iron phosphate (LFP), lithium manganese iron phosphate and lithium-supplement cathode materials for EV and energy-storage batteries. He is the company's core technology inventor and largest individual shareholder, and a deputy to the 14th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: He leads China's national nano energy-storage technology standards working group (SAC/TC279/WG7) and is an expert on ISO/IEC nanotechnology committees; Dynanonic now ships 4th-generation high-density LFP.
deep_cut_fact: Despite holding only a bachelor's degree, he is an external doctoral supervisor at Central South University and has won the China Patent Award and the title 'Guangdong Outstanding Inventor'.
notes: Strong fit for an energy-storage/battery-materials episode. Board secretary is He Yanyan (IR route). Likely needs Chinese-language outreach.

name: Trudy Shan Dai
current_role: Alibaba co-founder; former CEO of Taobao & Tmall Group (until Dec 2023), then tasked with setting up Alibaba's asset-management company; left the Alibaba Partnership in FY2025. Current title not confirmed.
profile: Hainan-born engineer and one of Alibaba's 18 founders (1999) who ran customer service, built the B2B telephone sales force, and later led Alibaba.com, China domestic digital commerce and Taobao/Tmall. Her fortune stems mainly from Ant Group holdings. Replaced by Eddie Wu at Taobao/Tmall in 2023 and moved to help build Alibaba's asset-management arm; exited the partnership in 2025.
interesting_fact: The telephone sales team she built for Alibaba.com's B2B business in 2003-05 reportedly generated about 60% of Alibaba's revenue every year until 2010.
deep_cut_fact: In Alibaba's earliest days she ran customer service working 16-18 hour days; her team answered emails so fast customers doubted they were real people. She joked: 'Whenever my department is on the right track, I know I'm about to be assigned to a new position.'
notes: Very private, rarely interviewed. Alibaba group media contacts are corporate; her current link to Alibaba is reduced (exited partnership 2025), so press team may not represent her.

name: Prachak Tangkaravakoon
current_role: Founder of TOA Paint (Thailand) PCL; stepped down as chairman in Feb 2024 for health reasons (no current executive role)
profile: Founder of TOA, Thailand's largest paint company (around half the decorative market) with plants across Southeast Asia. He grew a family hardware business into paint supplies in 1964 and opened the first paint factory in 1972; the company IPO'd in 2017 raising $360m. Operations are run by his children; son Jatuphat is CEO.
interesting_fact: The Tangkaravakoon family started by importing TOA paint from Japan before building their own Thai manufacturing; he co-founded the business with his wife Laor.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as a hardware store; he expanded into paint supplies in 1964 and opened the first TOA paint factory in 1972.
notes: Retired from board in 2024 citing health; outreach better directed to CEO Jatuphat Tangkaravakoon via TOA. directors@ is the board contact channel published in the 2025 sustainability report.

name: Henadiy Boholyubov
current_role: Co-owner, Privat Group (Ukraine); former co-owner of PrivatBank
profile: Ukrainian businessman (also spelled Gennadiy Bogolyubov) who co-founded PrivatBank with Ihor Kolomoyskyy in the early 1990s and built the Privat Group conglomerate with interests in ferroalloys, fuel stations and energy. PrivatBank was nationalised in 2016; he reportedly left Ukraine in 2024.
interesting_fact: PrivatBank, founded with about $1m of capital, grew to handle more than a third of Ukraine's private deposits and serve about half the population.
notes: Not recommended for outreach: UK High Court ordered him and Kolomoyskyy to pay PrivatBank over $3bn (2025, appeal lost 2026); sanctioned in Ukraine (Feb 2025) and subject to Ukrainian criminal proceedings. Sources: https://privatbank.ua/en/news/2025/11/10/former-owners-ordered-to-pay-privatbank-over-us-3-billion

name: Pier Luigi Loro Piana
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Loro Piana (LVMH-controlled Italian luxury textiles and fashion house)
profile: Sixth-generation member of the Piedmont wool family who, with his late brother Sergio, ran Loro Piana for decades and turned the fabric maker into a global luxury brand built on rare fibres (vicuña, baby cashmere, lotus). The brothers sold 80% to LVMH in 2013; he remains deputy chairman and a prominent maxi-yacht racer.
interesting_fact: A lifelong sailor, he races his maxi yacht 'My Song' (latest in a series of boats with that name) at events such as the Loro Piana Giraglia, competing again in 2025 and 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1990s he had the idea of separating the ultra-fine under-fleece of Mongolian kid goats (baby cashmere) into its own fibre, launching what the company calls a 20-year development effort.
notes: Approach via Loro Piana/LVMH corporate communications; no personal channels found. Sailing (My Song) is a strong rapport topic.

name: Bruce Gordon
current_role: Owner of WIN Corporation (WIN Television) and Birketu Pty Ltd; retired from boards in Aug 2024 but remains Birketu's ultimate decision-maker
profile: Sydney-born (1929) media owner who went from vaudeville magician and theatre manager to 30 years as a Paramount Television programming/sales executive, then bought Wollongong's WIN TV from Rupert Murdoch in 1979 and built it into Australia's largest regional TV network. Through Birketu he is a major Nine Entertainment shareholder; WIN co-owns the St George Illawarra Dragons.
interesting_fact: He is one of nine living Australians to have appeared on every AFR Rich List since it began in 1984, and was made an Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he juggled fruit to draw customers to his father's street-side fruit stall in Surry Hills, and he kept honing his magic act into his 20s, debuting on Sydney's Tivoli theatre circuit, where he got to know Rupert Murdoch and the Packers.
notes: Aged 97 and retired from boards; famously private. WIN TV contact page is regional/station-level, not personal. Low likelihood of participation.

name: Raymond Zage
current_role: Founder and CEO, Tiga Investments (Singapore); director and major shareholder of Grindr (NYSE: GRND)
profile: Illinois-born (1970) investor who spent eight years at Goldman Sachs and then built Farallon Capital's Asian business, leading deals such as the post-crisis Bank Central Asia stake and Aston Resources (later merged into Whitehaven Coal). He founded Singapore-based Tiga Investments in 2017, led the 2020 buyout of Grindr from Kunlun and took it public via his Tiga SPAC; in 2025 he and James Lu made an $18/share take-private bid, later withdrawn.
interesting_fact: He was an early backer and board member of Indonesian super-app Gojek, and has served as an independent director of Toshiba.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the board of the Singapore American School Foundation, has served on the National University of Singapore's investment committee, and has been active with literacy charity Room to Read.
notes: Energy angle: as a Farallon partner he led the Aston Resources coal investment (Whitehaven Coal). No published press contact found for Tiga Investments; Grindr IR is the closest corporate route but he is not an executive there.

name: Hu Jinsheng
current_role: Director and co-actual controller, Zhejiang Starry Pharmaceutical (SSE: 603520); re-appointed to the board May 2026
profile: Born 1955 in Xianju, Zhejiang, Hu built Starry Pharmaceutical into a leading Chinese maker of iodinated contrast-media APIs and injections (iohexol, iopamidol, iodixanol) plus quinolone APIs and CDMO services. He was chairman and GM from 2004, chairman until 2022, and handed the chair to his son Hu Jian; father and son are joint actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Starry's core products are X-ray/CT contrast agents and their API intermediates, a niche where it is one of China's major suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: Before pharmaceuticals he ran a paint business: he was director of the Xianju County paint factory and chairman/GM of Taizhou Qihutu (lacquer) before leading Starry from 2004.
notes: Low public profile; Chinese-language outreach via company board secretary (Zhang Yi) through the official site. Not an energy/data-center fit.

name: Chen Jianmin
profile: Listed by Hurun (2017-2022) as a property developer with wealth from 'Guangda', jointly with Chen Runguang. Could not confirm which 'Guangda' company (possibly Dongguan-based Guangdong Guangda Group / Guangda Real Estate, founded 2002 from a 1993 Dongguan predecessor) or any biographical details.
notes: Identity not verified: the name is common (also a Hong Kong sociologist of the same name, unrelated). Possible link to Guangdong Guangda Group (Dongguan) is unconfirmed; would need Chinese business-registry check.

name: Jennifer van der Leegte
current_role: Member of the main management (executive board), VDL Groep, Eindhoven
profile: Daughter of Wim van der Leegte and part of the second family generation running VDL Groep, the Eindhoven industrial group (buses incl. electric buses, contract manufacturing such as Mini/BMW car assembly at VDL Nedcar, defence and high-tech parts). With brothers Willem (CEO) and Pieter she joined the top management on 1 Jan 2016; the family has said VDL will remain private and family-owned.
interesting_fact: VDL was founded by her grandfather Pieter van der Leegte in 1953 and grew under her father Wim into one of the Netherlands' largest family industrial companies; it opened an electric-bus plant in Roeselare, Belgium in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Per a 2017 Trends profile she headed environment and HR at VDL; her father described his three children as 'Pieter the mouth, Jennifer the doer (de doener), Willem the brain'.
notes: Press route: Miel Timmers, VDL Groep communications director and spokesperson. Electric buses / manufacturing angle fits an energy-transition episode; Willem is the usual public face.

name: Jose Llado Fernandez-Urrutia
profile: Founder (1960) of Spanish engineering contractor Técnicas Reunidas, former Spanish minister and ambassador to the US (1978-82). He died in February 2024 aged 89; his son Juan Lladó Arburúa leads the company.
notes: Deceased Feb 2024. Source: https://www.deia.eus/economia/2024/02/15/muere-empresario-exministro-jose-llado-7875619.html . For the podcast, Técnicas Reunidas (now CEO/Executive Chairman Juan Lladó) is active in power generation for data centers, a possible alternative guest.

name: Austin Russell
current_role: Founder, Russell AI Labs (AI/frontier-tech builder and investor, launched Oct 2025); founder and former CEO of Luminar Technologies
profile: Newport Beach-born (1995) optics prodigy who conceived Luminar's lidar at 17, left Stanford with a Thiel Fellowship in 2012, and took Luminar public via SPAC in Dec 2020, briefly becoming the world's youngest self-made billionaire at 25. He stepped down as CEO in May 2025; Luminar filed for Chapter 11 in Dec 2025. He now runs Russell AI Labs, which says it took a stake in agentic-AI firm Emergence.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes he developed the idea for Luminar at 17 and became the youngest self-made billionaire at 25 after its Nasdaq listing.
deep_cut_fact: On 1 January 2022 he donated $4 million to the YouTuber-led #TeamSeas ocean clean-up campaign, pushing it over its $30 million goal; in 2021 he gave $70 million to the Central Florida Foundation.
notes: Sensitive: resigned from Luminar in 2025 after a board ethics inquiry, failed buyback bid, Luminar bankruptcy and related litigation; likely below billionaire status now. Avoid these topics in outreach; frame around AI/Russell AI Labs.
